Flat Bottom Vessel on Concrete and Grout
Most commonly used for FRP Tanks
Can be used for metal tanks in special cases
Includes pressurized vessels e.g. Chlorate Reactor

Polyethylene Tank on Concrete and Sand
For large polyethylene tanks such as the ones made by “Snyder”

Flat Bottom Tank on Steel
Generally for smaller tanks on skids - steel plate supports bottom
Can include pressurized tank e.g. Catholyte Tank

Flat Bottom Tank on Concrete no Grout
Used for most metal tanks
Skirt Supported Vessel on Concrete Ring Wall

Skirt Supported Vessel on Concrete Pad
Used for smaller diameter vessels
Diaphragm Pump on Concrete and Grout
Centrifugal Pump on Concrete and Grout
Plate & Frame Exchanger on Concrete and Grout

Horizontal Vessel on Concrete and Grout
Consider thermal expansion when calculating distance between anchor bolts.
